title: Proof: what REAL cmux default keys that macOS also holds do (Ctrl-Cmd-D Look Up, Ctrl-Cmd-S hot key 4, Shift-Cmd-F hot key 157), with a real Cmd-D as the control
why: STATUS 1649, cmux-ad 14:50Z: in the real-key smoke round a real Ctrl-Cmd-D made no New Column, while debug.key Ctrl-Cmd-D passed 10/10; very likely macOS's system hotkey 70 'Look up in Dictionary' (Ctrl-Cmd-D, on by default) takes the key before cmux. This journey records, for a real Cmd-D (control) and then a real Ctrl-Cmd-D: whether cmux's key router saw the key at all, which action ran (the app's action log), which other apps' windows are on screen (a Look Up panel), and a full-display screenshot right after the key. Needs a whole-host lease on a CuaDriver-granted mini. Added (New Column key lead aef4f4e6f83f36107, STATUS 1819): the window server's live table also has hot key 4 (Ctrl-Cmd-S, cmux saveLayoutTemplate) and 157 (Shift-Cmd-F, cmux findInDirectory) ON; each probe records the router count, the action log, the windows and a screenshot. The mini's com.apple.symbolichotkeys is never changed.
